bullets.title: Semis broadly sold off: SOXX -4.5%, Korea KOSPI -5.8% on memory inflation & valuation fears
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector saw a sharp risk-off session with SOXX down 4.54% pre-market; Korea's KOSPI fell 5.8% on LLM IPO concerns and demand-destruction fears from consumer electronics price hikes. Major declines: WDC -7.1%, MU -6.8% (after prior +16% post-earnings), AMD -4.6%, ARM -5.2%, AVGO -3.0%, TSM -2.6%, INTC -4.3%. Citi formally downgraded Semis to Market Weight from Overweight, citing strong fundamentals but much already priced in.

bullets.title: AAPL -6%: 15-20% price hikes on Macs/iPhones signal memory cost pass-through, demand risk debated
bullets.body: Apple announced 15-20% price hikes on high-volume SKUs due to soaring memory/storage costs (MSFT also raising Xbox prices 23% on 2.5x memory cost jump). AAPL bulls argue carrier/installment plan demand inelasticity and generous margins; bears flag demand destruction risk and trajectory of memory pricing into next year. iPhone 18 builds reportedly unchanged, but a new CEO ascension Sept 1 adds further uncertainty.

bullets.title: MU +16% post-earnings validates memory supercycle; SCAs limit upside surprise but GMs ~85-86%
bullets.body: Micron's blowout earnings (exact figures in prior session) drove a +16% rally that revived the AI memory trade, though the stock subsequently pulled back with the broader semi selloff. Strategic Customer Agreements cover >50% of revenue with floor pricing and prepayments; UBS sees gross margins normalizing to mid-50s vs. historical ~35%. Klein notes Q4 2026 buyback catalysts and sees $130-145B annual FCF potential; SCA structure limits volatility on upside surprises.

bullets.title: SNDK F2Q26 massive beat; PT raised to $325 on hyperscaler ramp convergence
bullets.body: SanDisk reported F2Q26 revenue of $19.6B (+31% YoY) and EPS of $4.14 vs. $4.03 consensus, with F3Q26 guidance raised to $18.6B revenue (+$1.8B vs. consensus) and $4.50 EPS (+$0.47 vs. consensus). JPM raised PT to $325; Hyve margins remain weighed by AI-server mix but expected to improve. Memory shortages worsening through 2026; Lenovo calls higher memory prices the 'new normal' into 2030.

bullets.title: Mag 7 down ~3%: FCF transfer to memory suppliers, OpenAI delays, open-source competition cited
bullets.body: MSFT, AMZN, META, GOOGL fell ~3% on concerns over hyperscaler FCF value transfer to memory suppliers and geopolitical AI risks. Additional headwinds: US government asked OpenAI to stagger GPT-5.6 release (opaque approval process), OpenAI deferring IPO to 2027, and Chinese open-source LLMs (Z.ai GLM-5.2) narrowing the gap on frontier models. 22V notes all Mag 7 names are below their 50-day MA with only 3 above the 200-day MA.

bullets.title: NVDA: Supply chain dismisses Vera Rubin doubts; GB300 on track for 3Q26; AMZN GPU prices +20% July 1
bullets.body: NVDA's supply chain sources pushed back on Vera Rubin concerns, with the GB300 transition described as on track for 3Q26 ramp. Amazon is raising GPU instance prices +20% on July 1 across Blackwell/Hopper/Ampere fleet, a signal of continued pricing power in AI compute. NVDA pre-market down ~0.9% with broader semi weakness but fundamental narrative intact per sell-side.

bullets.title: DKNG: DKeX launched; June PM volumes $200M+, up 80% m/m; JPM maintains Overweight
bullets.body: DraftKings launched DKeX, its proprietary prediction markets exchange, completing a vertically integrated PM stack. June consumer PM volumes tracking $200M+, up 80% from May's $110M; week of 6/21 saw $11.3B annualized total trading volume ($3.4B consumer, 2.6x May). JPM maintains Overweight; ~30% of customers using combos, which now represent ~15% of PM consumer volume. 2Q results unlikely to be dragged by higher PM investment despite OSB headwinds.

bullets.title: ORCL: Largest OpenAI counterparty faces near-term overhang on IPO delay and regulatory uncertainty
bullets.body: With OpenAI deferring its IPO to 2027 and the US government imposing an opaque approval process on frontier model releases, ORCL—identified as having the largest counterparty exposure to OpenAI—is seen facing near-term share price overhang. ORCL shares have been trending down since earnings; Chinese LLM advancement during this regulatory pause adds further uncertainty to the AI infrastructure demand thesis.

bullets.title: SNOW: TimesSquare nearly doubled position post-Cortex Code launch; Q2 FY27 guidance 30% YoY growth
bullets.body: A TimesSquare PM described Snowflake as critical foundational AI infrastructure, noting that over 50% of customers adopted Cortex Code within 9 weeks of launch—a catalyst not reflected in guidance. Q2 FY2027 guidance: $1.41-1.42B product revenue (30% YoY), 12.5% non-GAAP operating margin; FY2027 revenue guide $5.84B (31% YoY), 75% gross margin. Position nearly doubled on conviction that enterprise AI data modernization is in early innings.

bullets.title: AMD: Server CPU revenue path to ~$50B by 2030E per UBS; ARM favored in latency-sensitive head nodes
bullets.body: UBS raised its AMD server CPU revenue estimate toward ~$50B by 2030 (up from $41B prior), driven by AI rack buildout. ARM is seen as advantaged in latency-sensitive head node applications while AMD dominates throughput-focused AI rack configurations. Enterprises are focusing on token efficiency and cost controls rather than cutting AI deployment, supporting both names.

bullets.title: AVGO: JPM hosting virtual NDR with CEO Hock Tan on July 7; market cap $1.80T
bullets.body: JPMorgan scheduled a virtual non-deal roadshow for Broadcom on July 7, 2026, with CEO Hock Tan and CFO Amie Thuener participating. No new fundamental claims released; AVGO pre-market down ~3.0% with broader semi weakness.

bullets.title: Russell 2026 recon: Record $244B turnover; NVDA upweight to $4.23B; AAPL/AMZN/MSFT shift Growth→Value
bullets.body: The Russell 2026 reconstitution (effective June 26 close) is the largest in history at ~$244B notional turnover vs. $151B in 2021. NVDA's R1000 Growth upweight surged from $1.96B to $4.23B notional trade. AAPL, AMZN, and MSFT shift from Growth to Value and are the largest net sell names; GOOGL, MU, and AMD see Value-to-Growth shifts. Communication Services expected to receive $11.7B in passive inflows; Consumer Discretionary faces $9.5B outflows.

bullets.title: TSLA: 2Q delivery estimate raised to 416k (+7.6% y/y) on Europe strength
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its Tesla 2Q delivery estimate to 416k units (+7.6% YoY) from a prior 373k estimate (-2.8% YoY), citing strong European registrations up 47% YoY in April after a weak 2025. Full-year 2026 ESS deployment forecast remains at 55 GWh (+18% YoY), below consensus.

bullets.title: Citi: Downgrades Tech & Semis to MW; upgrades Software to MW from Underweight
bullets.body: Citi made sector-level rating changes this morning: Semis downgraded to Market Weight from Overweight (fundamentals strong but priced in) and broader Tech downgraded to Market Weight from Overweight. Software upgraded to Market Weight from Underweight, a notable shift that aligns with the view that AI-related software beneficiaries (productivity apps, data platforms) are better positioned on a risk/reward basis.

bullets.title: Streaming survey: Netflix strongest retention; AAPL TV+ engagement declined y/y; MS OW on DIS, NFLX, PSKY
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 16th annual streaming survey shows Amazon Prime Video, Netflix, and YouTube remain the top 3 platforms with overall adoption up YoY. Netflix had the strongest net retention score; Apple TV+ engagement declined year-over-year. Morgan Stanley is Overweight DIS, NFLX, and PSKY; Equal-weight WBD and STRZ; Underweight AMCX.

bullets.title: STX/WDC: HDD bull case strongest in years; 20-30% pricing upside per TB from HAMR; $80-100 STX EPS by CY27/28
bullets.body: Klein flagged HDDs as the most bullish near-term case in semis/storage: HAMR drives could deliver 20-30% pricing upside per TB, with potential for $80-100 STX EPS and $50-60 WDC EPS in CY27/28. WDC pre-market down 7.1-9.3% with broader tech selloff, creating a potential setup against the fundamental thesis.

bullets.title: ACN: $2B buyback boost to $7.5B (~10% of mkt cap); Q4 buyback rate $2.3B
bullets.body: Accenture announced a $2B increase to its buyback program bringing the total to $7.5B, representing ~10% of market cap and a 62% YoY increase in program size. The Q4-Aug-26 buyback run rate is $2.3B, signaling management confidence in free cash flow generation per UBS.

bullets.title: BE/grid: US datacenter power headroom approaching zero by 2027; behind-the-meter power a marginal solution
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's TMT note flagged that US datacenter power headroom is approaching zero and turns negative by 2027, making behind-the-meter power solutions increasingly critical. BE is identified as a Russell rebalance net-sell name (R2000→R1000 promotion), creating technical selling pressure today independent of fundamentals.

bullets.title: NET/DASH/PSKY: Russell promotion names flagged as net sells today; broader software setup improving
bullets.body: Cloudflare (NET), DoorDash (DASH), and PSKY are flagged as Russell rebalance net-sell names due to R2000→R1000 promotions effective today. Separately, DKNG +2.6% pre-market on DKeX launch. Citi's upgrade of Software to Market Weight suggests improving sector-level tailwind post-rebalance.

bullets.title: BKNG/EXPE: US RevPAR +9.7% YoY, +5.9% QTD with World Cup adding 400bps; Marriott/Hilton both tracking above guidance
bullets.body: US lodging RevPAR surged 9.7% YoY (week ended June 20) with the World Cup contributing ~400bps; luxury chain scale up 17.4%, urban markets +18.4%. Marriott tracking +3.4% QTD vs. 1.5-2.5% guidance; Hilton +3.4% vs. 2-3% guidance. US-Mexico passenger data flagged as weak, an area Expedia called out last quarter.
